title: Scale degrees and formulas
description: Drill degree numbers, alterations against major, functional names, and string-6 relative locations.

cards.front: What is a scale degree? What is a formula?
cards.back: A degree is a note’s position in the scale from the root: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7. A formula is a list of degrees, often with alterations, that describes a structure without naming any root.

cards.front: What is the major scale’s formula, and how are other structures described?
cards.back: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7. Everything else is how it differs from that reference: ♭3 lowers degree 3 of the major scale by a half step; ♯4 raises degree 4; ♭7 lowers degree 7.

cards.front: Are alterations measured against the previous note or against the major scale?
cards.back: Always against the major scale on the same root. In A, degree 3 is C♯ so ♭3 is C; degree 7 is G♯ so ♭7 is G.

cards.front: Why does a formula hold for any root while a note name holds for only one?
cards.back: Formulas separate structure from pitch. 1 3 5 is root, major third, fifth in every key. Build the major scale from the chosen root, then pick or alter degrees.

cards.front: How is a degree number also an interval from the root?
cards.back: Degree 3 is a third above, degree 5 a fifth above. Quality comes from the half steps the major scale gives, then from any alteration. A formula can be read as scale positions or as intervals.

cards.front: Name degrees 1–7 by their functional names.
cards.back: 1 tonic, 2 supertonic, 3 mediant, 4 subdominant, 5 dominant, 6 submediant, 7 leading tone.

cards.front: What is the role of tonic, mediant, subdominant, dominant, submediant, and leading tone?
cards.back: Tonic: home, rest. Mediant: halfway to the fifth; sets major or minor. Subdominant: leans down toward 3. Dominant: strongest support for the tonic. Submediant: relative minor lives here. Leading tone: half step under tonic in major.

cards.front: Give the degree formulas for a major triad, minor triad, and dominant seventh.
cards.back: Major 1 3 5. Minor 1 ♭3 5. Dominant seventh 1 3 5 ♭7.

cards.front: Root on string 6 at fret r (r at least 1). Where are degrees 3, ♭3, 4, 5, and the octave?
cards.back: 3: string 5, fret r−1. ♭3: string 5, fret r−2. 4: string 5, fret r (same fret). 5: string 5, fret r+2. Octave: string 4, fret r+2.

cards.front: From G on string 6 fret 3, locate degrees 3, 4, 5, and the octave.
cards.back: 3 is B at string 5 fret 2. 4 is C at string 5 fret 3. 5 is D at string 5 fret 5. Octave G is string 4 fret 5. All match G major (G A B C D E F♯).

cards.front: Translate 1 3 5 in C, G, D, and F.
cards.back: C E G. G B D. D F♯ A. F A C.

cards.front: Translate 1 ♭3 5 in C, G, D, and F.
cards.back: C E♭ G. G B♭ D. D F A. F A♭ C.

cards.front: Translate 1 2 3 5 in C, G, D, and F.
cards.back: C D E G. G A B D. D E F♯ A. F G A C.

cards.front: Translate 1 3 ♯4 5 in C, G, D, and F. Why is ♯4 B in F?
cards.back: C E F♯ G. G B C♯ D. D F♯ G♯ A. F A B C. In F the fourth is B♭, so ♯4 is a half step above that: B.

cards.front: Write degrees 1–7 for G major and F major.
cards.back: G A B C D E F♯. F G A B♭ C D E.

cards.front: What is degree 5 in E, A♭, B♭, and F♯?
cards.back: B, E♭, F, C♯.

cards.front: In A, name 1 ♭3 5 ♭7.
cards.back: A C E G.

cards.front: In E, name 1 2 ♭3 4 5.
cards.back: E F♯ G A B.

cards.front: Which degree of D major is C♯? Which degree of B♭ major is A?
cards.back: Both are degree 7.

cards.front: Root C on string 6 fret 8. Find and name degree 3, 5, and the octave.
cards.back: String 5 fret 7 (E), string 5 fret 10 (G), string 4 fret 10 (C).

cards.front: What is ♭7 of E, and where is it on string 6?
cards.back: D, string 6 fret 10.
